conditions: The target is a Linear team.
The team's visibility is private (not public).
The team's description mentions distributed systems.
Priya Nair is added as a member of that team.

readings: The description must contain the literal phrase "distributed systems".
The description must be topically about distributed systems, even if it uses different wording (e.g. "distributed computing", "distributed architecture").
Case-sensitive match on the key's leading characters (e.g. must be "ENG..." in uppercase).
Case-insensitive match, so a key like "eng-platform" would also qualify.

turn2.differences: The author's c1-c3 map cleanly onto my step-1 conditions for private, key prefix, and description content. Adding Priya Nair is the action performed once the team is found, not a matching condition, so its absence from c1-c3 is expected. One caveat: verifying c2 relies on inference from naming/elimination rather than an explicitly visible privacy field in the truncated data.

ambiguity_effects.explain: Could mean the literal phrase or a topical paraphrase. Makes no practical difference here since matching descriptions use the literal phrase and the failing one (t-ds-guild) is unrelated to the topic either way.
Case sensitivity is a theoretical ambiguity but all keys are uppercase, so it selects the same teams either way.

turn2.naturalness_note: A real user would typically just name the team directly rather than identify it via a key-prefix filter plus description-content filter; this compound phrasing reads like something built to force checking near-miss records.
